QF.id: Retirement Planning Products: National Pension System (NPS)_34

question.text: Per the chapter text on page 122 of the NISM Series XVII Retirement Adviser workbook (June 2025), what is the minimum subscription period stated for premature exit from NPS?

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter text on p. 122 of the NISM Series XVII Retirement Adviser workbook (June 2025) states that premature exit from NPS is allowed only after at least 10 years of subscription. Anchored to that chapter text, the keyed answer is 10 years. The Trap: Option B (5 years) is defensible under the regulatory excerpt on p. 257 of the same workbook, which states a subscriber before age 60 with no employer-employee relationship may voluntarily exit after at least 5 years. The audit flagged this internal conflict between the chapter text and the regulatory excerpt. Option A (3 years) is the threshold for subscribers who join after age 65. Option C (7 years) has no source basis. Note: The original stem read as a general current-rule question, which the workbook itself answers inconsistently (p. 122 vs p. 257). The stem now explicitly anchors the question to the chapter text on p. 122, so option D (10 years) is uniquely correct. Candidates relying on the regulatory excerpt or current PFRDA rules may encounter the 5-year figure in practice.
